name: Question 6
problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/7094d1527f7feb9dac54cbd90e595dcbb71c11d5c0a32d1371c3c63c54127899.png)

Change the order of integration in the integral

$$
{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{x}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1-y}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x
$$

so that it is integrated first with respect to $y,$ then $z,$ and then $x.$ The integration region $R$ is shown above.
worked_solution:
We wish to find limits of integration ${u}_{1}(x,z),$ ${u}_{2}(x,z),$ ${v}_{1}(x),$ ${v}_{2}(x),$ $a,$ and $b$ such that

$$
{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{x}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1-y}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(x)}^{{v}_{2}(x)}{\int }_{{u}_{1}(x,z)}^{{u}_{2}(x,z)}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x.
$$

From the repeated integral, we see that the region of integration $R$ can be written as a type I region as follows:

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,\,x\le y\le 1,\,\,0\le z\le 1-y}
$$

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x$ to $\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x,$ we write $R$ as a type III region and its projection $D$ onto the $xz$-plane as a type I *plane* region.

To visualize this, imagine firing an arrow through the region parallel to the $y$-axis and in the direction of increasing $y,$ as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/c48de52085373361c4e4de3010ebe36c1da702f0efec45b455dff891869086f2.png)

The arrow enters the region through the left boundary and leaves through the right boundary:

- The left boundary of the region, written in the form $y=y(x,z),$ is

$$
x=y\,⟹\,y=x
$$

- The right boundary of the region is

$$
z=1-y\,⟹\,y=1-z.
$$

Therefore, the type II representation of $R$ is

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(x,z)\in D,\,\,x\le y\le 1-z},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/fd5d71a6d6509851e5131fe458b9672d59eb7ff6c07499949ae199b45f4ddae0.png)

Now, we consider the projection $D$ as a type I plane region in the $xz$-plane with the top curve given by

$$
{\begin{aligned}y=1-z \\ y=x\end{aligned}\,⟹\,x=1-z\,⟹\,z=1-x.
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/12743c492a7f7883a2ecd8d3ca73138a324a53040cb8936f4794f9e8d84c8fd5.png)

Hence, we have that

$$
D={(x,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,\,0\le z\le 1-x}.
$$

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration so that it is integrated first with respect to $y,$ then $z,$ and then $x,$ we obtain

$$
{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{x}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1-y}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1-x}{\int }_{x}^{1-z}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x.
$$

Question 6
?

Change the order of integration in the integral ∫01∫x1∫01−yf(x,y,z)dzdydx so that it is integrated first with respect to y, then z, and then x. The integration region R is shown above.

a
 ∫01∫01−x∫0zf(x,y,z)dydzdx
b
 ∫01∫01−x∫x1−zf(x,y,z)dydzdx
c
 ∫01∫01∫xzf(x,y,z)dydzdx
d
 ∫01∫0x∫01−zf(x,y,z)dydzdx
e
 ∫01∫0x∫z1−xf(x,y,z)dydzdx
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We wish to find limits of integration u1(x,z), u2(x,z), v1(x), v2(x), a, and b such that

∫01∫x1∫01−yf(x,y,z)dzdydx=∫ab∫v1(x)v2(x)∫u1(x,z)u2(x,z)f(x,y,z)dydzdx.

From the repeated integral, we see that the region of integration R can be written as a type I region as follows:

R={(x,y,z):0≤x≤1,x≤y≤1,0≤z≤1−y}

To change the order of integration from dzdydx to dydzdx, we write R as a type III region and its projection D onto the xz-plane as a type I plane region.

To visualize this, imagine firing an arrow through the region parallel to the y-axis and in the direction of increasing y, as shown below.

The arrow enters the region through the left boundary and leaves through the right boundary:

  • The left boundary of the region, written in the form y=y(x,z), is x=y⟹y=x

  • The right boundary of the region is z=1−y⟹y=1−z.

Therefore, the type II representation of R is R={(x,y,z):(x,z)∈D,x≤y≤1−z}, as shown in the diagram below.

Now, we consider the projection D as a type I plane region in the xz-plane with the top curve given by {y=1−zy=x⟹x=1−z⟹z=1−x.

Hence, we have that D={(x,z):0≤x≤1,0≤z≤1−x}.

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration so that it is integrated first with respect to y, then z, and then x, we obtain

∫01∫x1∫01−yf(x,y,z)dzdydx=∫01∫01−x∫x1−zf(x,y,z)dydzdx.
